points: Object storage keeps a small index of where each object lives apart from the large pile of drives that hold the bytes.
Facebook found that per-photo file metadata was the bottleneck, so it packed photos into large files and kept the offsets in memory.
Amazon spreads each object's erasure coded shards over its own set of drives so no customer's reads land on a few hot disks.
Dropbox groups blocks into buckets, runs one Master per cell, and adds capacity by adding cells.

figures.label: Drive capacity has improved 7.2 million times since 1956, seek time only 150x
28% less cost per usable terabyte than the NAS design
A typical cell holds 50 PB of raw data

prerequisiteReasons.replication: Object stores keep several copies or coded shards of every object, so replication explains why redundancy is needed and what it costs in space and repair work.
prerequisiteReasons.sharding: Object stores spread keys and data over many drives and cells, so sharding explains how data is split across machines and why balance matters.
